findings.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in Registration Name Field — Django Templates
findings.description: The user-supplied 'name' field in the multi-step registration form is evaluated directly as a Django template string rather than being safely passed as a context variable. The step3 page renders the name inside a <script> tag using DjangoTemplates. An attacker can inject Django template syntax ({% debug %}, {{ flag }}, etc.) to extract sensitive context variables including the application flag. The template context contains a 'flag' variable with the CTF flag.

reproduction.command:
1. GET /accounts/register/step1/ to obtain CSRF token
2. POST name={{flag}}&password=testpassword123 to /accounts/register/step1/
3. POST email=x@x.com to /accounts/register/step2/
4. GET /accounts/register/step3/ - flag appears in <script>alert() output
